messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: X'X matrix is singular.
parts:
That warning message is saying that one of the many linear regression fits was over-specified; that may happen if one of the possible genotypes is missing.

You can generally ignore this, but if you get odd LOD curves (for example, _really_ large values), this may be the cause.

karl


> When analyzing this population with scanone I will sometimes get the following warning,
>
> Warning messages:
>
> 1: X'X matrix is singular.
>
>
>
> However, this only occurs with specific traits. When I look at distributions of the phenotypes they appear normal.
>
> I can still pull up summary information but I get a high LOD (>100) for the specific trait that throws the warning. I guess I'm wondering what to do about further analysis for the potential QTL?
>
>
> Thanks

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: X'X matrix is singular.
parts:
Are you using scanone with method="em" (the default)?

If so, then this is coming up during the process of the iterative algorithm. And the progress of that algorithm (and potential difficulties) would be different for different phenotypes.

karl

Warning message of "Jacobian matrix is singular" was given when using scanone. out<- scanone (geno,pheno.col=pheno.col,model="binary",addcovar=block). Can you tell me what should I do to solve this problem?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: X'X matrix is singular.
parts:
The problem is similar to the "X'X is singular problem"; an issue in fitting the logistic regression model. Usually these issues occur in regions where there's no evidence for a QTL anyway, so they can generally be ignored.

Look at a plot of the LOD curves. If there are extremely high LOD score, be suspicious. If things look reasonable, then don't worry.

karl
